reviews.body:
Thank you. The fix is correct: a journey that is not kept now removes the older `last-journey`, and the test drives the exact case from the issue. One small change, then this can merge.

Rule 3 says no free strings. The text `the last journey did not verify yes; nothing to keep` is written in `act-sequence-tool.ts` and again in the test. Put it in one named constant (next to `JOURNEY_RECORDING` is a good place), use it in both places, and push.
Thank you. `JOURNEY_NOT_KEPT` sits next to `JOURNEY_RECORDING`, and the tool and the test both use it. This merges when CI passes.

comments.body: Thanks for your first pull request to Reticle! A maintainer aims to review within two days. Before then, `pnpm verify` locally catches most of what CI will, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reticlehq/reticle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the rest. If CI does not start, a maintainer needs to approve it for first-time contributors; that is normal.

Done: the message is now `JOURNEY_NOT_KEPT`, next to `JOURNEY_RECORDING`, and both the tool and the test use it.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
